svg.data-overall-dimensions: 166 x 177 x 48.3 mm including protrusions (datasheet; body modelled from CAD is 160 x 45.32 x 165)
svg.data-poe-per-port: max per PSE class: 8 ports at PoE 15.4 W, 7 at PoE+ 30 W, 2 at PoE++ 90 W
svg.data-power-supply: dual USB-C power adapter, or PoE++ up to 90 W input via the PD port
svg.data-optics-sfp-plus: vendor optics line per the ReadyLinks Optics datasheet: SFP-1/10G-MM, SFP-1/10G-SM, SFP-1/10G-SM-SF-23 and -SF-32 (BiDi) 1/10G transceivers; no third-party support statement published

Deliberately drawn plain; only symmetric content, axis noted per the symmetric-face rule."},"chassis":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing (GLB body extents 160.0 x 45.32 x 165.0 mm W/H/D; front face is the +x plane of the GLB scene, face width = scene z extent). The datasheet states 166 x 177 x 48.3 mm overall (6.55 x 6.95 x 1.9 in) - the deltas are per-axis (3.7/7.3/6.0 percent), NOT a uniform scale factor, so they are protrusions and mounting furniture outside the metal body (wall-mount bosses, jack noses, feet), not a unit error. The modelled body is the GLB metal; the datasheet overall is recorded here, unresolved per-axis, in the spirit of body-between-the-ear-folds."},"front-layout":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - every position measured from GLB mesh bounding boxes in face coordinates (x from left as in the vendor render, y down from top). Jack columns at x 92.6/106.5/120.5/134.5 (13.95 mm pitch), rows at y 15.3/28.8; stacked rows are mirrored - the render at 15.96 px/mm zoom shows the TOP row keyway-UP (rotate 180 from the std default) and the bottom row keyway-down; a first draft had it inverted and only the zoomed crop settled it. SFP pair is belly-to-belly with its four lamp band at y 21.7; the 2.5G pair is one tall stacked connector in one tall shell (GLB shell face 60.1..77.3 x 7.3..34.5; contact strips at y 15.2-18.2 and 23.7-26.7 place the mouths at centres ~13.5 and ~28.4, so the BOTTOM 2.5G jack nearly aligns with the GbE bottom row while the top one sits ~1.8 mm above the GbE top row - the maintainer's review caught the first draft placing the pair too high); the silver ganged-connector shells (two 58.4 x 14.9 row strips and the 2.5G shell) are drawn as decor per the s9510-28dc silver-band precedent, since std/rj45-ganged draws the opening only (the USB-C receptacles get the same treatment - the real parts are silver shells on the black face, so a silver pill sits behind each std/usb-c slot, which the maintainer's review asked for after the bare slots vanished into the background; row-shell VISIBLE faces photo-measured at 9.0 px/mm - 13 mm flanges starting y 9.2/22.4, so the port lamps sit on black above and below them as the render shows; the GLB 14.9 mm figure is the cage body behind the panel); USB-C pair at x 25.3; status lamps at x 12.7, y 22.2/26.9/32.0; reset button at (150.1, 30.2). The render confirms every feature and the port legends. Eight of the ten jacks (the GbE/PoE row pair) are drawn with std/rj45-ganged@2 (12.7 x 11.0, the bezel-less opening); the other two, the 2.5G pair, are the same 12.7 x 11.0 cell lamped - common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 - because the GLB jack bodies are 13.4 mm on a 13.95 mm pitch inside one ganged shell strip per row (58.4 x 14.9 in the GLB) - std/rj45's 16 mm bezel physically cannot sit on that pitch, which L39 proved by overlap before the swap."},"pd-port-identity":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet lists '(1) 2.5G RJ45 port (1) 2.5G RJ45 PoE PD port' but no document says whether 2.5G1 or 2.5G2 is the PD port - registered as a gap; neither placement claims the PD role."},"port-leds":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - 3.0 mm lenses above the top jack row (y 6.4) and below the bottom row (y 37.2), one per column; datasheet 'ReadyLighting: 64 color LED per port'. Drawn with common/led-dot (2.0 mm) - lens reads 3.0 mm in the GLB, the closest library part is used and the delta recorded here."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - 'Maxpower consumption 20W (Excluding PoE output) 240W (Full PoE load)'; power-max-w carries the 240 W full-PoE-load figure (envelope fully-configured, which is what a budget needs) and power-self-max-w the 20 W excluding-PoE-output figure. PoE budget 218 W max at 25 C. Input 44-56 V DC 1.86 A is the PoE-PD electrical spec; supply is dual USB-C adapters or PoE++ up to 90 W in."},"rear-layout":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - the GLB rear is the finned end cap (15 mm deep, full width) with no connectors, openings or printing; drawn as a rib field. Content is symmetric, so the horizontal axis convention could not be exposed by any feature - noted per the symmetric-face rule."},"sfp-leds":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - four 2.0 mm lamps in the cage centre band at y 21.7, x 41.5/44.3/47.9/50.8; the 3.6 mm gap splits them into pairs. WHICH pair belongs to which cage is stated nowhere - assigned by adjacency (left pair to the top cage XG2, right pair to XG1) and registered as a gap."},"side-layout":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - both sides are 15 mm finned heatsink walls running the full depth (GLB side blocks 156.3 x 45.0 x 15.0). Drawn as rib fields. An unidentified 9.2 x 10.2 x 7.7 mm boss sits on the right side wall near the front (GLB idx22, y 7.9-18.1) - likely a security-slot or mount boss, identity stated nowhere, NOT drawn; registered as a gap. On a RIGHT view x=0 is the front; on a LEFT view x=0 is the rear."},"silkscreen":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"photo-measured - legends transcribed from the vendor front render (RL/SYS/PWR, USB1/USB2, XG1/XG2, 2.5G1/2.5G2, port numerals: even ports numbered above the top row, odd below the bottom row; the XG/2.5G labels join their ports through one BRACKET per row - a horizontal bar under the label pair with a vertical drop to each port, per the vendor 3D view the maintainer supplied - not four separate leaders). The ReadyLinks wordmark is printed as plain text like the halny HALNY precedent; the render's wifi-arc logo graphic is deliberately not reproduced (community-skin logo rule)."},"sources":{"note":"vendor GLB 3D model (KeyShot CAD export, gl-8xep.glb - 728 nodes, 435k triangles, per-part meshes at millimetre scale), vendor datasheet (ReadyLinks-GL-8xEP-Datasheet.pdf, converted), vendor front render (photos/gl-8xep-1-front.png), catalog API snapshot (gen/readylinks-catalog.json). First device in the library modelled with vendor CAD geometry as the position source."},"stack-orientation":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 1 SFP pair (xg2/xg1). 1 of these were drawn with the upper cage turned before the std cage art moved its lip to the bottom of the opening; turning them keeps the lips in the middle band where they were drawn and seats every optic bail-outward."},"top-layout":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - lid plate (150.3 x 147.7 inset) with six 5.3 mm torx screws in a 3x2 pattern; positions from GLB screw meshes. Axis convention: y=0 is the REAR of the chassis, y=165 the front, matching the halny top-view precedent.
